# What Heroku API tokens the library redacts, and what it leaves alone.
#
# Every token here is built from the ordered run 0123456789abcdef, which no real
# credential is. A body in the shape Heroku writes a token in now is sixty
# base64url characters, so the run three times over and twelve more is one, and
# the prefix in front brings a token to sixty-five. A body in the shape it wrote
# one in until 23 April 2025 is a UUID, the same run cut into the groups
# 8-4-4-4-12, so such a token is forty-one.

patterns: heroku-api-token

# The one prefix Heroku writes a token with, in the places a token is written.
# There is a single kind of string here rather than a table of them: an
# authorization created from the CLI, an access token minted by the OAuth flow
# and the key the dashboard prints are the same credential in the same Bearer
# header, and nothing on one says which of them it came from.

case:     a token in an environment assignment
in:       HEROKU_API_KEY=HRKU-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab
out:      HEROKU_API_KEY=«heroku-api-token»

case:     a token in the header the platform api reads it from
in:       Authorization: Bearer HRKU-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab
out:      Authorization: Bearer «heroku-api-token»

case:     a token in the netrc entry the cli writes
in:       machine api.heroku.com\n  login me@example.com\n  password HRKU-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab
out:      machine api.heroku.com\n  login me@example.com\n  password «heroku-api-token»

case:     a token in the json an authorization returns
in:       {"access_token":"HRKU-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab","expires_in":28799,"token_type":"Bearer"}
out:      {"access_token":"«heroku-api-token»","expires_in":28799,"token_type":"Bearer"}

case:     a token on a curl command line
in:       curl -H "Authorization: Bearer HRKU-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab" https://api.heroku.com/apps
out:      curl -H "Authorization: Bearer «heroku-api-token»" https://api.heroku.com/apps

case:     a token in what the cli prints on creating an authorization
in:       Token:       HRKU-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab
out:      Token:       «heroku-api-token»

# The shape Heroku wrote a token in until the length changed, which is the
# prefix in front of a UUID. Those tokens were never revoked — Heroku said at
# each change that current tokens keep working until they are regenerated, and
# an authorization created from the CLI does not expire — so both shapes are
# read. What tells a UUID from any other thirty-six characters written behind
# the prefix is that its four separators stand at fixed places, and its
# hexadecimal is read in either case.

case:     a token in the shape written until the length changed
in:       HRKU-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef
out:      «heroku-api-token»

case:     the same token with its hexadecimal in uppercase
in:       HRKU-01234567-89AB-CDEF-0123-456789ABCDEF
out:      «heroku-api-token»

case:     a uuid whose separators stand elsewhere
in:       HRKU-0123456-789ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef
out:      HRKU-0123456-789ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef

case:     a uuid with a group past hexadecimal
in:       HRKU-0123456g-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef
out:      HRKU-0123456g-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef

case:     thirty-six hexadecimal characters with no separators
in:       HRKU-012345678901234567890123456789012345
out:      HRKU-012345678901234567890123456789012345

case:     a uuid whose separators are underscores
in:       HRKU-01234567_89ab_cdef_0123_456789abcdef
out:      HRKU-01234567_89ab_cdef_0123_456789abcdef

# A UUID is written in base64url, so a token of the shorter shape stands at the
# front of any longer one whose first thirty-six characters fall that way, and
# both readings are true of the same text. The longer one is walked first, so
# such a token is redacted once at sixty-five characters rather than as the
# forty-one inside it with twenty-four characters of a live token left beside
# them. Where the longer reading fails the shorter is taken all the same.

case:     a token whose body opens on a uuid is one value and not two
in:       HRKU-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «heroku-api-token»

case:     a uuid with too few characters behind it for the longer reading
in:       HRKU-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef0123
out:      «heroku-api-token»0123

# The alphabet the sixty characters are written in: the whole of base64url, which
# is what both rules reading this format admit. Heroku states the prefix and the
# length and states no alphabet, so a body carrying either character base64url
# adds is a body, and one carrying anything outside it is no body at all.

case:     a body carrying an underscore
in:       HRKU-0123456789abcdef_123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab
out:      «heroku-api-token»

case:     a body carrying a hyphen
in:       HRKU-0123456789abcdef-123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab
out:      «heroku-api-token»

case:     a body carrying a dot
in:       HRKU-0123456789abcdef.123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab
out:      HRKU-0123456789abcdef.123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab

case:     a body carrying an equals sign
in:       HRKU-0123456789abcdef=123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab
out:      HRKU-0123456789abcdef=123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab

case:     a body carrying a space
in:       HRKU-0123456789abcdef 123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab
out:      HRKU-0123456789abcdef 123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab

# The two characters both rules reading this format ask for at the front of a
# body, which this pattern does not. Heroku states the prefix and the length and
# does not state them, so a body opening on them and a body opening on anything
# else are both read: being wrong about two characters nobody wrote down would
# locate no token at all.

case:     a body opening on the two characters the rules ask for
in:       HRKU-AA0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789
out:      «heroku-api-token»

case:     a body opening on anything else
in:       HRKU-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab
out:      «heroku-api-token»

case:     a body written in capitals
in:       HRKU-0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789AB
out:      «heroku-api-token»

# The lengths either side of sixty. That count is Heroku's own, stated as a
# sentence on its OAuth page, and it is used as a count rather than a floor:
# fifty-nine characters are not a token, and sixty-one are a token and one
# character that belongs to no credential. The second of those is the price of
# having no boundary behind the match — a boundary there would drop this token
# rather than trim it, and a real token written against a digit would come
# through whole.

case:     a body of sixty characters is a token
in:       HRKU-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab
out:      «heroku-api-token»

case:     a body of fifty-nine characters is not
in:       HRKU-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      HRKU-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a

case:     an alphabet run longer than a token is a token and what follows it
in:       HRKU-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcd
out:      «heroku-api-token»cd

# What a token may be written against. The prefix is the whole of the anchor and
# there is no boundary on either side of it, so a token keeps its span whatever
# word character it abuts.

case:     a token after an underscore
in:       HEROKU_API_KEY_HRKU-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab
out:      HEROKU_API_KEY_«heroku-api-token»

case:     a token after a letter
in:       xHRKU-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab
out:      x«heroku-api-token»

case:     a hyphenated word written against a token
in:       HRKU-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab-suffix
out:      «heroku-api-token»-suffix

case:     a token at the end of a sentence
in:       the token is HRKU-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab.
out:      the token is «heroku-api-token».

# Two tokens written together, and a token written inside one. Every character
# of the prefix is written in the body's own alphabet, so a whole prefix can
# stand anywhere inside a body: the scan advances a byte at a time rather than
# stepping over what it took, and where the two values overlap the redaction
# reaches from the first character of the outer one to the last of the inner.

case:     two tokens with nothing between them
in:       HRKU-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abHRKU-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab
out:      «heroku-api-token»«heroku-api-token»

case:     a token opening at the first character of another body
in:       HRKU-HRKU-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab
out:      «heroku-api-token»

case:     a token of each shape on one line
in:       new=HRKU-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab old=HRKU-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef
out:      new=«heroku-api-token» old=«heroku-api-token»

case:     two tokens of the shorter shape with nothing between them
in:       HRKU-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdefHRKU-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef
out:      «heroku-api-token»

case:     a token between japanese
in:       日本語HRKU-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab日本語
out:      日本語«heroku-api-token»日本語

case:     a token after an invalid byte
in:       \xffHRKU-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab
out:      \xff«heroku-api-token»

case:     a token followed by a carriage return and a newline
in:       HEROKU_API_KEY=HRKU-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab\r\n
out:      HEROKU_API_KEY=«heroku-api-token»\r\n

case:     a token between tabs
in:       \tHRKU-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab\t
out:      \t«heroku-api-token»\t

case:     a token in a yaml value
in:       api_key: HRKU-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab
out:      api_key: «heroku-api-token»

case:     a token in a query string
in:       https://api.heroku.com/apps?token=HRKU-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab&page=2
out:      https://api.heroku.com/apps?token=«heroku-api-token»&page=2

case:     a token cut short with an ellipsis
in:       HRKU-0123456789abcdef0123456789...
out:      HRKU-0123456789abcdef0123456789...

case:     one token per line over three lines
in:       a=HRKU-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab\nb=HRKU-0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789AB\nc=HRKU-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab
out:      a=«heroku-api-token»\nb=«heroku-api-token»\nc=«heroku-api-token»

# What this pattern redacts that nobody issued. The alphabet holds the hyphen,
# so an unbroken run of hyphenated words is a body and sixty of them behind the
# prefix are redacted; no count of unbroken letters rules that out, because a
# hyphen never ends the run. What holds it back is the four capitals in front,
# which spell no word and which no kebab-case name written by a tool begins
# with. Sparing these would mean narrowing the alphabet, and that would decline
# every token whose body fell with a hyphen in it.

case:     a hyphenated run long enough to be a body
in:       HRKU-alpha-bravo-charlie-delta-echo-foxtrot-golf-hotel-india-juliet
out:      «heroku-api-token»et

case:     a hyphenated run the count stops short of
in:       HRKU-alpha-bravo-charlie-delta-echo-foxtrot-golf
out:      HRKU-alpha-bravo-charlie-delta-echo-foxtrot-golf

# And what this pattern leaves alone. The first three are the prefix, which is
# read in the case Heroku writes it and with every character of it. Then the two
# shapes Heroku's own pages print with nothing in front of them, both left in
# the output whole: the refresh token handed out beside an access token is a
# bare UUID, and the example the authentication page writes its netrc entry with
# is forty hexadecimal characters, which is neither shape on record — what the
# CLI stores in that field today is the OAuth token the changelogs prefixed, and
# the netrc case at the top of this file is one. Neither carries the prefix the
# whole of this pattern rests on, and what is left of each is a shape this
# library may not read: a UUID is an identifier written in URLs and dashboards
# by design, and forty hexadecimal characters are a SHA-1.

case:     a lowercase prefix
in:       hrku-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab
out:      hrku-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab

case:     the prefix without the hyphen closing it
in:       HRKU0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abc
out:      HRKU0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abc

case:     an underscore where the prefix closes
in:       HRKU_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab
out:      HRKU_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab

case:     a refresh token beside an access token
in:       {"refresh_token":"01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef"}
out:      {"refresh_token":"01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef"}

case:     the older shape the netrc example is written in
in:       0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     a run of the right length opening with no prefix
in:       xxxxx0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab
out:      xxxxx0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab

case:     prose
in:       there is no credential in this sentence
out:      there is no credential in this sentence

# And the text a token is written among, which this pattern has nothing to say
# about. The prefix is four capitals and a hyphen, so what reaches the byte the
# scan searches for is uppercase text, and the vendor's own host name and CLI
# are written in lowercase throughout.

case:     a log line naming the api a token authenticates against
in:       time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="deploying release" app=acme-web url=https://api.heroku.com/apps/acme-web/dynos
out:      time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="deploying release" app=acme-web url=https://api.heroku.com/apps/acme-web/dynos

case:     the command line an authorization is created from
in:       heroku authorizations:create --description "ci deploy"
out:      heroku authorizations:create --description "ci deploy"

case:     the config a token is set into
in:       heroku config:set --app acme-web DEPLOY_TARGET=production
out:      heroku config:set --app acme-web DEPLOY_TARGET=production
